The only WebView (HelpActivity) enables JavaScript but sets allowContentAccess = false and never enables universal file URL access.
HelpActivity sets allowFileAccess = false and does not enable setAllowFileAccessFromFileURLs or setAllowUniversalAccessFromFileURLs (minSdk 26, defaults false).

The 'Private note' field (content the app encrypts at rest because it is sensitive) is a plain OutlinedTextField with default keyboard options, so the keyboard may learn/cache it. The password uses OutlinedSecureTextField.

evidence.detail: Private note field has no non-caching keyboard options (autoCorrect/keyboardType left at defaults).

fills.reason: Internal navigation uses an explicit Intent (HelpActivity.intent). Implicit intents are only ACTION_VIEW to the browser/privacy policy and ACTION_SEND choosers, which are intentionally external; no broadcasts or services.
Implicit intents with extras are ACTION_SEND wrapped in createChooser for user-initiated sharing (share-link text, receipt image via FileProvider read grant); no tokens or credentials in extras.

Backup rules exclude only sharedpref credentials.xml, session.xml and unlock.xml. Needs a backup/restore run. Statically, auth prefs are excluded but receipts.db, receipt photos and the plaintext CSV in files/backup are included; decide whether these count as sensitive.

The exported HelpActivity only shows public help pages from https://help.pennyjar.example in a WebView; it shows no account data, performs no security action and doesn't bypass the biometric lock (its bridge exposes only appVersion and close).
Security values (biometric secret, share-link token) use SecureRandom; the only kotlin.random.Random use picks an avatar colour in AvatarColors.
No time-based values (currentTimeMillis, Date, Calendar) used for tokens, keys or IVs; IVs come from the Keystore cipher and tokens from SecureRandom.
The only key generation is AES with setKeySize(256) in KeystoreKeys; no RSA/EC key pairs.
All Cipher.getInstance calls use AES/GCM/NoPadding; no DES, 3DES, RC4 or Blowfish.
All symmetric encryption uses GCM mode (AES/GCM/NoPadding); no ECB or bare 'AES' transformation.
BiometricGate.isAvailable calls BiometricManager.canAuthenticate(BIOMETRIC_STRONG), which requires a secure lock screen, before enabling or using the app lock.
No asymmetric key pairs (KeyPairGenerator) are generated; only AES encrypt/decrypt keys.
Providers are named only as AndroidKeyStore (KeyStore.getInstance and KeyGenerator.getInstance for Keystore keys); Cipher.getInstance uses the default provider.
BiometricPrompt allows only BIOMETRIC_STRONG; DEVICE_CREDENTIAL and setDeviceCredentialAllowed are not used.

BiometricPrompt.authenticate is called with a CryptoObject whose key has setUserAuthenticationRequired(true). Note: the session token key (TokenStore) is not auth-bound, so the lock protects the UI, not the token.
The biometric key is created with setInvalidatedByBiometricEnrollment(true).
PromptInfo.Builder never calls setConfirmationRequired(false); the default (confirmation required) applies.
The biometric key uses setUserAuthenticationParameters(0, AUTH_BIOMETRIC_STRONG) on API 30+ and setUserAuthenticationValidityDurationSeconds(-1) below, i.e. per-use authentication.
No SSLContext.getInstance, setEnabledProtocols or OkHttp ConnectionSpec configuration; both OkHttp clients use library defaults.
The only http:// URL is the debug buildConfigField API_BASE_URL (10.0.2.2); release uses https, and other endpoints in Endpoints.kt, ShareLinks and HelpActivity are https.
No SSLSocket or SSLSocketFactory use; all networking goes through OkHttp.
No custom X509TrustManager or checkServerTrusted implementation in the sources.
No custom HostnameVerifier; OkHttp's default verifier is used.
HelpActivity's WebViewClient overrides only shouldOverrideUrlLoading; onReceivedSslError is not overridden, so SSL errors cancel by default.
No ProviderInstaller.installIfNeeded(Async) call and no Play Services dependency; network clients are created in Application.onCreate without updating the security provider.

evidence.detail: HTTP clients are initialised without a prior security provider update.
